name: IEDB_predict_mhci_binding
description: Predict MHC class I peptide binding using NetMHCpan via the IEDB next-generation tools API (https://api-nextgen-tools.iedb.org). Given a protein sequence and HLA allele, predicts which peptides will bind and be presented on the cell surface. Returns one row per scored peptide with the method's own score/IC50 and percentile columns, plus a uniform 'percentile_rank' (lower = stronger binding), sorted strongest first. Essential for vaccine design, neoantigen prediction, and epitope mapping. Supports human HLA-A/B/C and mouse H2 alleles. The prediction runs asynchronously upstream and typically returns within about 15 seconds.

sequence.description: Protein sequence (amino acid letters, e.g., 'TYQRTRALVFQRTRALKMFAL'). Multiple peptides can be concatenated. A FASTA block (starting with '>') is also accepted.

allele.description: MHC allele name, validated upstream against the MHC Restriction Ontology. Human: 'HLA-A*02:01', 'HLA-B*07:02'. Mouse: 'H2-Kd', 'H2-Db' (the legacy 'H-2-Kd' spelling is accepted and translated). Comma-separate for several alleles. Default: HLA-A*02:01

name: IEDB_predict_mhcii_binding
description: Predict MHC class II peptide binding using NetMHCIIpan via the IEDB next-generation tools API (https://api-nextgen-tools.iedb.org). Predicts CD4+ T helper cell epitopes. Given a protein sequence and HLA-DR/DP/DQ allele, returns one row per scored sliding-window peptide with the method's own core/score/percentile columns plus a uniform 'percentile_rank' (lower = stronger binding), sorted strongest first. Essential for vaccine design (helper epitopes) and autoimmunity research. The prediction runs asynchronously upstream and typically returns within about 15 seconds.

sequence.description: Protein sequence (amino acid letters). A FASTA block (starting with '>') is also accepted.

allele.description: MHC-II allele, validated upstream against the MHC Restriction Ontology. Examples: 'HLA-DRB1*01:01', 'HLA-DRB1*15:01'. Comma-separate for several alleles. Default: HLA-DRB1*01:01

length.description: Sliding-window peptide length scored within 'sequence' (11-30, default 15). Cannot exceed the sequence length; omit to use 15, or the sequence's own length when that is shorter.

name: IEDB_predict_bcell_epitopes
description: Predict linear B-cell (antibody) epitopes along a protein sequence using the IEDB B-cell tool (default BepiPred). Scores every residue and returns the contiguous regions predicted to be antibody-accessible epitopes, plus the per-residue scores. Use for vaccine antigen design and antibody target selection. Example: a viral surface protein sequence returns its predicted surface-exposed epitope stretches.

sequence.description: Protein amino-acid sequence (single-letter codes), e.g. an antigen of interest.

name: IEDB_predict_antigen_processing
description: Predict MHC class I antigen processing using the IEDB next-generation tools API (https://api-nextgen-tools.iedb.org). Unlike raw binding prediction, this runs the NetCTLpan processing predictor alongside an MHC-I binding predictor, chaining proteasomal cleavage + TAP transport + MHC-I binding into a combined score that identifies peptides likely to be naturally processed and presented to CD8+ T cells. Returns one row per peptide with cleavage_prediction_score, tap_prediction_score, mhc_prediction and combined_prediction_score (sorted highest first), alongside the binding method's own IC50/score and percentile columns. Use for neoantigen and epitope prioritization beyond binding affinity. Sequences of 20 or more residues are recommended, since cleavage prediction needs flanking context. No authentication required.

sequence.description: Protein sequence (single-letter amino acids), e.g. 'SLYNTVATLYCVHQRIDVKQNTLKLATGGKS'. 20+ residues recommended. Aliases: sequence_text.

allele.description: MHC class I allele, validated upstream against the MHC Restriction Ontology. Human: 'HLA-A*02:01', 'HLA-B*07:02'. Mouse: 'H2-Kd' (the legacy 'H-2-Kd' spelling is accepted and translated). Default: HLA-A*02:01

method.description: MHC-I binding method used in the chain: 'netmhcpan' (default), 'netmhcpan_ba', 'netmhcpan_el', 'ann', 'smm', 'smmpmbec', 'comblib_sidney2008', 'consensus'.

sequence_number.description: Which submitted sequence this peptide came from, 1-based (1 on all 23 rows of the single-sequence example). Several sequences can be submitted at once and the rows are returned interleaved in score order, so this is the only thing that says which protein a peptide belongs to.

length.description: Peptide length in residues (9 on all 23 rows of the example, which asked for 9-mers). A run that asks for several lengths returns them mixed together in one score-ordered list.

peptide_index.description: The peptide's 1-based rank within this sequence, 1 for the best-scoring (1..23 over the 23 rows). The rows arrive sorted by combined_prediction_score, so this is the rank the sorting produced.

percentile_rank.description: The PROCESSING percentile rank from NetCTLpan: where this peptide's combined cleavage+TAP+binding score falls among random peptides, so smaller is better. Coarse-grained -- 2.0, 3.0, 6.0, 16.0, 32.0, 50.0 over the 23 rows, capped at 50. This is NOT the binding percentile; binding.netmhcpan.percentile ran 0.41 to 96.0 on the same rows.

binding.netmhcpan.core.description: The 9-residue binding core NetMHCpan aligned into the MHC groove. ONE property whose name contains dots -- it is not a nested object. Equal to the peptide on all 23 rows of the example because they are all 9-mers; for a longer peptide it is the sub-sequence that actually sits in the groove.

binding.netmhcpan.icore.description: The 'interaction core': the core plus any residues NetMHCpan judged to bulge out of the groove, i.e. the stretch a T-cell receptor would see. A dotted NAME, not a path. Equal to core on all 23 example rows; it differs when the peptide is longer than the groove.

binding.netmhcpan.ic50.description: NetMHCpan's predicted binding affinity in nM, ranging 46.5 to 45779.76 over the 23 example rows; under ~500 nM is the usual binder threshold. A dotted NAME, not a path. The tool's own description promises the binding method's IC50 and this is it -- mhc_prediction is the method's rescaled score, not an affinity.

binding.netmhcpan.percentile.description: NetMHCpan's BINDING percentile rank, 0.41 to 96.0 over the 23 example rows, smaller being a stronger binder. A dotted NAME, not a path. Identical to median_percentile on all 23 rows because only one binding method ran; with several methods the median is taken across them and the two part.
